newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slip, seen drifting.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slip, seen drifting.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 0.98 percent on low volume on Thursday as fresh capital continued to steer clear and traders held out little hope of a revival over the short term.
"Currently there is not enough domestic money on the market for continuous growth and foreign buying is blocked," said Bojan Sekavcnik, a trader at brokerage PM & A.
The SBI index fell 13.33 points or 0.98 percent to 1,340.65.
Fears are growing that a glut of new listings within the next month may dilute already poor liquidity, he added.
Among the companies that are expected to be listed in April is petrol trading firm Petrol, among Slovenia's five biggest companies.

"Until there is fresh capital from abroad, which may take over a month, shares will stagnate. I expect the index will go up or down by a maximum of five percent next week," said Peter Krassnig, an analyst of bank Nova Ljubljanska Banka.

The central bank blocked international portfolio investment in February by saying foreign investors have to open custodian accounts at Slovenian banks in order to trade in shares. Since then the blue-chip index has lost more than 23 percent
Overall 10 shares fell, five rose and one was flat, while 11 were untraded. Turnover slumped to 57.6 million tolars from 92.8 million.
Construction company GPG led the day's decliners, tumbling 9.19 percent to 5,630 tolars on volume of 291 shares.

Market participants attributed the fall to the company's plans to expand the amount of shares listed and that it would have to stop trading for two weeks from April 14 in order to register the new shares at the central securities registry KDD.
Trading firm Kovinotehna's ordinary shares were the top gainers, jumping three percent to 480 tolars on volume of 931 shares. Traders said Kovinotehna rose on expectations of good business results.
Mineral water producer Radenska was the most active share, falling 2.15 percent to 1,954 tolars on volume of 7,642 shares.
Traders expect Radenska, listed a week ago, to rebound as the shares are perceived to be relatively cheap when considering the company's good earnings performance and prospects.
